title: Highest Net Migration Rate

source.name: UN DESA — World Population Prospects 2024 (Net Migration Rate)

note: Gulf states dominate due to labor migration policies where foreign workers greatly outnumber citizens. Small island states and post-conflict receiving countries can also rank high. Positive values mean more people arriving than leaving.
disclaimer: Gulf states dominate due to labor migration policies where foreign workers greatly outnumber citizens. Small island states and post-conflict receiving countries can also rank high. Positive values mean more people arriving than leaving.

title: Highest Elderly Share
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of population aged 65 and over.

source.name: World Bank — Population ages 65 and above (% of total)

note: Japan crossed 29% first and remains the world's most-aged large economy. Monaco tops microstates thanks to its high-income retiree base. The list is entirely developed high-income countries plus a couple of European microstates.
disclaimer: Japan crossed 29% first and remains the world's most-aged large economy. Monaco tops microstates thanks to its high-income retiree base. The list is entirely developed high-income countries plus a couple of European microstates.

title: Largest total energy consumers
prompt: Name the countries that consume the most total primary energy each year.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Primary energy consumption across all sources (oil, gas, coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables) measured in exajoules (EJ).
trivia: China and the United States together consume roughly 43% of the world's primary energy — more than the next 15 countries combined.

title: Highest energy consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest primary energy consumption per person.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy / Our World in Data

disclaimer: Primary energy consumption per capita in gigajoules (GJ). Excludes micro-states under 100k population.
trivia: Iceland's massive per-capita number is driven by cheap geothermal and hydro used for aluminium smelting — smelters consume roughly 70% of the country's electricity.

title: Highest electricity consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries whose people consume the most electricity each year on a per-capita basis.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Per-capita electricity consumption in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Excludes micro-states under 100k population.
trivia: Norway's high per-capita number is a mix of cold-climate heating and abundant cheap hydropower — over 90% of Norwegian electricity comes from hydro.

title: Largest hydroelectric generation
prompt: Name the countries that generate the most electricity from hydropower each year.

source.name: IEA / Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Annual electricity generation from hydroelectric plants (excludes pumped storage) in terawatt-hours (TWh).
trivia: China's Three Gorges Dam alone produces more hydroelectricity than any other single power station in the world — roughly 100 TWh in a good water year.

title: Largest geothermal capacity
prompt: Name the countries with the most installed geothermal power capacity.

source.name: IRENA — Renewable Capacity Statistics

disclaimer: Installed electrical generating capacity of geothermal power plants in megawatts (MW).
trivia: Iceland gets nearly a third of its electricity and virtually all of its space heating from geothermal — the highest geothermal share of any country in the world.

title: Largest biofuels producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most liquid biofuels (ethanol + biodiesel) each year.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Combined ethanol and biodiesel production measured in petajoules (PJ) of energy content.
trivia: Brazil's ethanol program dates to the 1975 Proalcool response to the oil crisis; today most cars sold in Brazil are flex-fuel and can run on E100 (pure ethanol).

title: Highest refined petroleum output
prompt: Name the countries that refine the most crude oil into petroleum products each year.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Refinery throughput (crude oil processed) measured in thousand barrels per day (kb/d). Not the same as crude production.
trivia: India's Jamnagar refinery complex (Reliance) is the largest single refining site in the world at ~1.24 million barrels per day.

title: Largest LNG exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most liquefied natural gas (LNG).

source.name: EIA / GIIGNL — Annual LNG Report

disclaimer: Liquefied natural gas exports measured in million tonnes per annum (MTPA). The United States overtook Australia and Qatar in 2023 to become the world's largest LNG exporter.
trivia: Qatar built its entire modern gas industry on the offshore North Field — the largest single natural gas reservoir on Earth, shared with Iran (where it's called South Pars).

title: Largest LNG importers
prompt: Name the countries that import the most liquefied natural gas (LNG).

source.name: EIA / GIIGNL — Annual LNG Report

disclaimer: LNG imports measured in million tonnes per annum (MTPA). Europe surged into the top of the import table after the 2022 pipeline gas cutoff from Russia.
trivia: Japan was the world's largest LNG importer for decades — the country built the first modern LNG import terminal at Negishi in 1969 and has almost no domestic gas.

title: Countries most reliant on coal for electricity
prompt: Name the countries whose electricity mix has the highest share of coal.

source.name: Ember — Global Electricity Review

disclaimer: Share of national electricity generation that comes from coal (%). Excludes countries with under 5 TWh annual generation.
trivia: South Africa's coal reliance is a legacy of the apartheid-era Sasol coal-to-liquids strategy — Eskom's aging coal fleet has driven the country's rolling blackouts ("load shedding") since 2008.

title: Largest textile exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of textiles (fabrics, yarns, and made-up textile articles) by value.

source.name: WTO — World Trade Statistical Review (Merchandise trade by product)

disclaimer: Textiles category (SITC 65 / HS 50-60) — fabrics, yarns, thread, and made-up articles. Apparel/garments are a separate category.
trivia: China's textile exports alone are worth more than the next four countries' combined and account for roughly 40% of world textile trade.

title: Largest apparel exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest exports of clothing (apparel and garments) by value.

source.name: WTO — World Trade Statistical Review (Clothing)

disclaimer: Clothing category (SITC 84) — finished apparel/garments. Excludes fabrics and yarns.
trivia: Bangladesh's ready-made-garment sector accounts for roughly 85% of its total exports and employs over 4 million people, most of them women.

title: Fashion weeks by prestige
prompt: Name the countries hosting the world's most prestigious fashion weeks.

source.name: Business of Fashion — Global Fashion Week Rankings

disclaimer: Ranked by industry influence, buyer/press attendance, and number of major houses showing. Includes the 'Big Four' plus notable second-tier weeks.
trivia: The 'Big Four' fashion weeks — New York, London, Milan, and Paris — run in that fixed sequence twice a year, a schedule set by the industry in the 1970s.

title: Largest cosmetics markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest cosmetics and personal-care markets by retail sales value.

source.name: Statista — Beauty & Personal Care market outlook

disclaimer: Retail sales value across skincare, haircare, makeup, fragrances, and personal care. USD, current exchange rates.
trivia: South Korea has the highest per-capita spend on cosmetics in the world, and K-beauty exports have grown roughly 20% annually since 2015.

title: Highest luxury goods spend per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita spending on personal luxury goods.

source.name: Bain & Company — Luxury Goods Worldwide Market Study

disclaimer: Personal luxury goods (apparel, leather, jewelry, watches, beauty), resident spending only — excludes tourism-driven purchases.
trivia: Switzerland's per-capita luxury spend is inflated by a high concentration of wealth and Geneva/Zurich being global watch-and-jewelry hubs.

title: Largest jewelry markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest jewelry markets by retail sales value.

source.name: Statista — Jewelry market outlook

disclaimer: Retail sales of fine and fashion jewelry. USD, current exchange rates.
trivia: India's jewelry market is disproportionately gold-heavy — households collectively hold an estimated 25,000+ tonnes of gold jewelry, the largest private stockpile of any country.

title: Largest watch industries
prompt: Name the countries with the largest watch-manufacturing industries by export value.

source.name: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH — annual watch export data

disclaimer: Ranked by finished-watch export value. Includes both mechanical and quartz watches.
trivia: Switzerland accounts for over half the world's watch exports by value despite producing only about 2% by unit — China makes the volume, Switzerland makes the margin.

title: Most Louis Vuitton stores
prompt: Name the countries hosting the most Louis Vuitton retail stores.

source.name: Louis Vuitton — store locator

disclaimer: Full-line Louis Vuitton boutiques (not counting concessions or temporary pop-ups).
trivia: Japan has more Louis Vuitton stores per capita than any other country outside France, a legacy of the brand's 1980s explosion in popularity among Japanese consumers.

title: Largest silk producers
prompt: Name the world's largest producers of raw silk.

source.name: FAO / International Sericultural Commission — global raw silk production

disclaimer: Raw silk (mulberry and non-mulberry) production, metric tonnes per year.
trivia: China and India together produce over 90% of the world's raw silk, and China alone has led global production for more than two millennia.

title: Largest wool producers
prompt: Name the world's largest producers of wool.

source.name: International Wool Textile Organisation (IWTO) — Market Information

disclaimer: Greasy wool production (all sheep breeds combined), metric tonnes.
trivia: Australia produces the highest-value wool in the world — Merino fleece from New South Wales and Victoria dominates the fine-wool market that feeds Italian luxury tailoring.

title: Highest chocolate consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita chocolate consumption.

source.name: Statista / International Confectionery Association — Chocolate consumption per capita

disclaimer: Kilograms of chocolate confectionery per person per year. European countries with long chocolate-making traditions dominate the top of this ranking.
trivia: The Swiss eat chocolate more than three times per week on average, and their country is also the world's largest exporter of premium chocolate by value.

title: Highest wine consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita wine consumption.

source.name: International Organisation of Vine and Wine (OIV) — State of the World Vine and Wine Sector

disclaimer: Litres of wine per person per year, all adults and children counted. Small European wine-producing countries lead per-capita rankings even though larger countries consume more in absolute volume.
trivia: Portugal has topped the OIV per-capita wine consumption table for most of the past decade, with domestic table wine still cheaper than bottled water in many cafes.

title: Highest spirits consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita consumption of distilled spirits (pure alcohol equivalent).

source.name: WHO Global Information System on Alcohol and Health (GISAH)

disclaimer: Litres of pure alcohol from spirits per person aged 15+ per year. Eastern European countries with strong vodka traditions dominate this category, though the WHO figures capture only recorded (taxed) consumption.
trivia: Belarus and Latvia have swapped the top spot repeatedly in recent WHO reports; both regularly clock over half of all pure-alcohol intake as spirits rather than beer or wine.

title: Highest sugar consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita sugar and sweetener consumption.

source.name: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook — Sugar consumption per capita

disclaimer: Kilograms of refined sugar equivalent per person per year, including sugar used in processed foods and beverages. Excludes non-caloric sweeteners.
trivia: The US Department of Agriculture estimates the average American consumes over 34 teaspoons of added sugar per day when soft drinks, sauces, and baked goods are counted.

title: Highest bread consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita bread consumption.

source.name: AIBI (International Association of Plant Bakers) — European Bread Market Report; Statista bread consumption estimates

disclaimer: Kilograms of bread and bakery products per person per year. Includes flatbreads and traditional loaves; excludes pastries and biscuits.
trivia: Turkey's national bread agency TMO reports that Turks eat bread with virtually every meal — a habit reinforced by state-subsidised loaves sold at municipal 'halk ekmek' kiosks.

title: Highest pasta consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita pasta consumption.

source.name: International Pasta Organisation (IPO) — Global Pasta Consumption Report

disclaimer: Kilograms of dry pasta per person per year, per IPO annual member surveys. Countries without a domestic pasta manufacturers' association may be underreported.
trivia: The IPO celebrates World Pasta Day every October 25th, a date chosen to mark the first World Pasta Congress held in Rome in 1995.

title: Highest fish and seafood consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita fish and seafood consumption.

source.name: FAO — Food Balance Sheets (Fish and seafood supply per capita)

disclaimer: Kilograms of fish and seafood (live-weight equivalent) available per person per year from the FAO Food Balance Sheet. Excludes aquatic plants and mammals.
trivia: The Maldives' national dish, garudhiya (tuna broth) with rice, reflects a fishing economy where skipjack tuna is caught almost entirely by traditional pole-and-line methods.

title: Highest cheese consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita cheese consumption.

source.name: International Dairy Federation (IDF) — World Dairy Situation report; USDA FAS

disclaimer: Kilograms of cheese consumed per person per year, including fresh and processed cheeses. Countries with strong dairy traditions typically lead this ranking.
trivia: France recognises over 1,600 distinct varieties of cheese; President de Gaulle once quipped that it was impossible to govern a nation with 246 kinds of it.

title: Highest bottled water consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita bottled water consumption.

source.name: Statista / Beverage Marketing Corporation — Global bottled water market report

disclaimer: Litres of bottled water per person per year, including still, sparkling, and flavoured. Tap-water safety concerns and hot climates both push consumption higher.
trivia: Mexican courts have repeatedly ruled that access to potable water is a constitutional right, yet millions of households still buy 20-litre 'garrafones' weekly because municipal tap water is not universally trusted.

title: Highest ice cream consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita ice cream consumption.

source.name: Statista / International Dairy Foods Association — Ice cream consumption per capita

disclaimer: Litres of ice cream and frozen desserts per person per year. Includes dairy and non-dairy frozen desserts sold at retail; excludes soft-serve served at restaurants.
trivia: New Zealand's per-capita lead is partly a summer-hemisphere effect and partly a dairy-industry one: Fonterra co-op members supply almost all the country's ice cream cream base.

title: Highest Female Labor Force Participation
prompt: Name the countries with the highest female labor force participation rate (share of women aged 15+ in the labor force).

source.name: World Bank — Gender Data Portal (ILO modelled estimates)

disclaimer: Uses the ILO modelled estimate of female labor force participation for ages 15+. Excludes very small dependent territories.
trivia: Rwanda and Burundi rank at the top largely because subsistence agriculture is overwhelmingly done by women and counts as economic activity in ILO's definition.

title: Most Women in National Parliament
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of women in the (lower or single) house of the national parliament.

source.name: Inter-Parliamentary Union — Parline (Women in Parliament)

disclaimer: Uses the lower or single chamber. Reserved seats and gender quotas are counted where they exist.
trivia: Rwanda has been #1 in this ranking since the 2003 constitution set a 30% minimum quota; the actual share has stayed above 60% every election since.

title: Most Women in Senior Management
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of women in senior and middle management positions.

source.name: ILOSTAT — Share of women in senior and middle management

disclaimer: Uses ILO's ISCO-08 major group 1 (managers) for the most recently available year per country. Some countries report only large-firm data.
trivia: Jamaica has topped the ILO managerial-share list for most of the last decade, ahead of every OECD country.

title: Highest Age at First Marriage (Women)
prompt: Name the countries where women marry latest, ranked by mean age at first marriage for women.

source.name: UN DESA — World Marriage Data 2019
source.asOf: UN WMD 2019 (latest available observation per country)

disclaimer: Mean age at first marriage for women, using each country's most recent census or vital-statistics observation. Cohabitation is not counted as marriage.
trivia: Sweden's high average is driven by pre-marriage cohabitation being the near-universal norm; couples often marry only after their first child is born.
asOfDate: UN WMD 2019 (latest available observation per country)

title: Highest Divorce Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest crude divorce rate (divorces per 1,000 people per year).

source.name: UN DESA — Demographic Yearbook (Crude Divorce Rate)
source.asOf: Most recent year available per country, 2019–2022

disclaimer: Crude divorce rate per 1,000 population. Does not adjust for marriage rate, so countries where cohabitation replaces marriage can look artificially low.
trivia: The Maldives has topped the global divorce ranking for most of the last two decades — a legacy of very informal Islamic marriage-and-divorce procedures that require no court involvement.
asOfDate: Most recent year available per country, 2019–2022

title: Highest Cohabitation Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of partnered adults living in unmarried cohabitation rather than marriage.

source.name: UN DESA — World Marriage Data (share cohabiting among partnered women 25-29)

disclaimer: Share of partnered women aged 25–29 who are cohabiting rather than legally married. Latin America and Nordic Europe dominate for very different cultural reasons.
trivia: In Colombia and Peru, informal 'unión libre' has been the majority form of partnership for decades and confers most legal rights of marriage.

title: Longest Paid Maternity Leave
prompt: Name the countries that provide the most weeks of paid statutory maternity leave.

source.name: ILO — Maternity and paternity at work database

disclaimer: Statutory paid maternity leave in weeks (regardless of replacement rate). Combined maternity + parental leave that must be taken by the mother is included; general shared parental leave is not.
trivia: Bulgaria's 58.6 weeks is the longest fully-paid maternity entitlement in the world; the payment stays at 90% of the mother's wage the entire time.

title: Longest Paid Paternity Leave
prompt: Name the countries that provide the most weeks of paid statutory paternity leave (father-specific, not shared parental).

source.name: OECD Family Database — PF2.1 Parental leave systems

disclaimer: Father-specific paid leave in weeks (father-quota and paternity leave; excludes shared parental leave that either parent can take).
trivia: South Korea and Japan technically offer the longest father-specific entitlements on paper, but under 15% of eligible fathers actually take the full leave.

title: Highest Teen Birth Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest adolescent birth rate (births per 1,000 women aged 15–19).

source.name: World Bank / UN Population Division — Adolescent fertility rate

disclaimer: Births per 1,000 women aged 15–19 per year. Sub-Saharan Africa dominates due to early marriage norms and low contraceptive prevalence.
trivia: Niger's adolescent birth rate is more than 300x higher than South Korea's — the widest development gap of any UN population indicator.

title: Earliest Same-Sex Marriage Legalization
prompt: Name the countries that legalized same-sex marriage earliest (by year of nationwide legalization).

source.name: Human Rights Campaign / Pew Research — Same-sex marriage timeline

disclaimer: Year of nationwide legal recognition of same-sex marriage (not civil unions). Rank 1 is the earliest.
trivia: The Netherlands' first legal same-sex marriages were performed at the stroke of midnight on 1 April 2001 by then-Amsterdam mayor Job Cohen.

title: Oldest still-in-force written constitutions
prompt: Name the countries with the oldest written national constitutions still in effect today.

source.name: Comparative Constitutions Project / IDEA International / Wikipedia — List of national constitutions

disclaimer: Ranked by year the current codified constitution first took effect. Amendments don't reset the clock; wholesale replacements (e.g. France's Fifth Republic) do.
trivia: San Marino's Statutes of 1600 predate every modern constitution but are usually excluded because they're a medieval charter rather than a modern-style codified constitution.

title: Largest national legislatures (total seats)
prompt: Name the countries with the largest national legislatures by total number of seats (combining both chambers where bicameral).

source.name: Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) — Parline database

disclaimer: Combines both chambers for bicameral legislatures. Excludes indirectly appointed advisory bodies that lack legislative power.
trivia: China's National People's Congress has nearly 3,000 delegates who meet in plenary only once a year; day-to-day work is done by its Standing Committee of about 175.

title: Smallest national lower houses
prompt: Name the countries with the fewest seats in their national parliament (or lower house where bicameral).

source.name: Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) — Parline database

disclaimer: Counts elected/appointed seats in the primary legislative chamber only. Microstates dominate; ties are broken alphabetically.
trivia: The Federated States of Micronesia's Congress has just 14 senators serving a population of about 100,000 — one legislator per ~7,000 residents.

title: Currently active sovereign monarchies
prompt: Name countries where a monarch is currently the head of state (excluding Commonwealth realms sharing King Charles III).

source.name: Wikipedia — List of current sovereign monarchies

disclaimer: Only sovereign states with a resident monarch as head of state are listed. Commonwealth realms whose head of state is King Charles III (Australia, Canada, etc.) are excluded to avoid double-counting.
trivia: There are 28 sovereign monarchies today, down from more than 100 a century ago; the Vatican is the world's only elective absolute monarchy.

title: Largest national cabinets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest cabinets (Council of Ministers) by number of full ministerial members.

source.name: Wikipedia — Cabinet size comparisons / IPU government structures

disclaimer: Counts full cabinet ministers (not junior ministers, ministers of state, or advisors). Sizes fluctuate with reshuffles; figures reflect the most recent stable composition.
trivia: North Korea's cabinet lists over 50 ministers because virtually every state-owned sector (coal, chemicals, machine-building) has a dedicated portfolio.

title: Highest minimum voting age (21 or older)
prompt: Name countries where the minimum voting age for national elections is 21 or higher.

source.name: IDEA International / CIA World Factbook — Voting age comparisons

disclaimer: Most countries set voting age at 18; a handful require 21 or higher. Ranked by minimum age (highest first), ties broken by population.
trivia: The UAE requires citizens to be 25 to vote in Federal National Council elections, and only about a third of Emirati citizens are enrolled in the electoral college at all.

title: Most UN Security Council vetoes cast
prompt: Name the permanent members of the UN Security Council who have cast the most vetoes in the council's history.

source.name: United Nations — Security Council veto records / Dag Hammarskjold Library

disclaimer: Only the five permanent members (P5) hold a veto. The Russian Federation inherited the Soviet Union's tally in 1991, and this ranking merges those into a single Russia/USSR total.
trivia: The Soviet Union cast 79 vetoes in the first 10 years of the UN's existence alone — earning foreign minister Andrei Gromyko the nickname 'Mr. Nyet.'

title: Countries with mandatory (compulsory) voting
prompt: Name countries where voting in national elections is legally compulsory for eligible citizens.

source.name: IDEA International — Compulsory Voting database

disclaimer: Includes only countries where compulsory voting is written into law, whether or not sanctions are actively enforced. Ranked roughly by strictness of enforcement, then alphabetically.
trivia: Australia has fined non-voters since 1924; turnout at federal elections has stayed above 90 percent every cycle since, one of the highest sustained turnouts in the democratic world.

title: Countries where head of state is directly elected
prompt: Name countries whose head of state (president) is chosen by direct popular vote rather than by parliament, electoral college, or hereditary succession.

source.name: IDEA International — Electoral System Design database

disclaimer: Includes presidential and semi-presidential systems where the president wins office through direct nationwide vote. Excludes parliamentary republics where the president is elected by the legislature.
trivia: France returned to direct presidential election in 1962 by referendum under de Gaulle — before that the president was chosen by an electoral college of parliamentarians and local officials.

title: Countries using proportional representation
prompt: Name countries whose national lower house is elected by a proportional representation (PR) system.

source.name: IDEA International — Electoral System Design database

disclaimer: Includes list-PR and single-transferable-vote systems for the primary legislative chamber. Excludes mixed-member systems where the PR tier is only compensatory, and excludes majoritarian systems.
trivia: The Netherlands has one of the purest PR systems in the world — the entire country is a single electoral district with a 0.67 percent threshold, which is why it routinely elects 15+ parties to parliament.

title: Highest diabetes prevalence
prompt: Name the countries with the highest age-adjusted prevalence of diabetes among adults aged 20-79.

source.name: International Diabetes Federation — Diabetes Atlas (11th ed.)

disclaimer: Age-adjusted prevalence in adults 20-79. IDF national estimates exclude micro-populations under 100,000 and rely on modelled data where surveys are absent.
trivia: Small Pacific island nations dominate the top of the list — a legacy of rapid post-war shifts from traditional diets to imported processed foods.

title: Lowest under-5 child mortality rate
prompt: Name the countries with the lowest under-five child mortality rate (deaths per 1,000 live births).

source.name: UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME)

disclaimer: Deaths of children under 5 per 1,000 live births. Rank 1 = lowest. Only countries with populations above 100,000 are included in the top-line rankings.
trivia: Iceland and Finland have led the world for a decade, both with near-universal early-pregnancy prenatal care and family nurse home-visit programmes.

title: Highest measles vaccination coverage
prompt: Name the countries with the highest measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) coverage among one-year-olds.

source.name: WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC)

disclaimer: Percentage of surviving infants receiving one dose of measles-containing vaccine. Ties are broken alphabetically and many high-performing countries report the same 99% ceiling.
trivia: Many countries have been at 99% for a decade — the WHO does not officially publish figures above 99% for individual countries, treating that as the practical ceiling for national programmes.

title: Longest healthy life expectancy (HALE)
prompt: Name the countries with the longest healthy life expectancy at birth — years of life expected to be lived in full health.

source.name: WHO Global Health Observatory — Healthy Life Expectancy (HALE) at birth

disclaimer: Years lived in full health, adjusting overall life expectancy for time spent in poor health. Both sexes combined.
trivia: HALE typically runs 8-10 years below total life expectancy — the top-ranked countries also tend to have the smallest 'unhealthy' gap.

title: Highest per-capita nurses and midwives
prompt: Name the countries with the most nurses and midwives per 10,000 population.

source.name: WHO Global Health Observatory — Nursing and midwifery personnel density

disclaimer: Nurses and midwives per 10,000 population, latest reported year per country. Definitions vary slightly by country reporting practice.
trivia: Norway and Finland train roughly one nurse for every 55 residents — more per capita than most countries train doctors.

title: Highest per-capita pharmacists
prompt: Name the countries with the most pharmacists per 10,000 population.

source.name: WHO Global Health Observatory — Pharmacists density (per 10,000 population)

disclaimer: Pharmacists per 10,000 population, latest reported year. Includes both community and hospital pharmacists where the country reports them jointly.
trivia: Malta's density is inflated by its very small population — around 800 pharmacists on an island of half a million.

title: Highest per-capita mental health workers
prompt: Name the countries with the most mental health workers (psychiatrists, psychologists, nurses, and social workers) per 100,000 population.

source.name: WHO Mental Health Atlas 2020

disclaimer: Total mental health workforce per 100,000 people, combining psychiatrists, psychologists, mental health nurses, social workers and other cadres. Some countries include care assistants; others do not.
trivia: The WHO reports a 40-fold gap between the top and median country in mental health workforce density.

title: Most organ donors per million
prompt: Name the countries with the most deceased organ donors per million population.

source.name: IRODaT — International Registry on Organ Donation and Transplantation

disclaimer: Deceased donors per million population (pmp). Excludes living donors. Opt-out consent systems dominate the top of the table.
trivia: Spain has led the global rankings every year since 1992 — the 'Spanish Model' of dedicated in-hospital transplant coordinators is now studied and copied worldwide.

title: Highest COVID-19 deaths per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most confirmed COVID-19 deaths per million population over the course of the pandemic.

source.name: Our World in Data — COVID-19 cumulative confirmed deaths per million
source.asOf: Cumulative through end of 2023 (reporting effectively ceased in most countries thereafter)

disclaimer: Confirmed COVID-19 deaths per million population, cumulative. Excess-mortality estimates would produce a different ranking; some countries with weak surveillance are almost certainly undercounted.
trivia: Peru's death rate reflects both a genuinely severe outbreak and one of the most aggressive death audits of the pandemic — the country revised its total sharply upward in 2021.
asOfDate: Cumulative through end of 2023 (reporting effectively ceased in most countries thereafter)

title: Highest COVID-19 vaccination rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of population that received a complete initial COVID-19 vaccination course.

source.name: WHO / Our World in Data — Share of population fully vaccinated against COVID-19

disclaimer: Share of total population (all ages) that completed the primary vaccination series. Boosters not counted here. Small states with populations under 100,000 are excluded.
trivia: Several countries technically exceeded 100% of their resident population fully vaccinated because they also inoculated migrant workers, cross-border commuters and tourists.

title: Most G20 summits hosted
prompt: Which countries have hosted the annual G20 Leaders' Summit the most times since its inception in 2008?

source.name: G20 — official summit history / Wikipedia aggregation
source.asOf: Through the 2024 Rio de Janeiro summit (South Africa hosts in 2025)

note: Counts host country for each Leaders' Summit from 2008 (Washington) through the 19th summit (Rio de Janeiro 2024). The 2010 Toronto and 2010 Seoul summits are counted separately, giving that year two hosts.
disclaimer: Counts host country for each Leaders' Summit from 2008 (Washington) through the 19th summit (Rio de Janeiro 2024). The 2010 Toronto and 2010 Seoul summits are counted separately, giving that year two hosts.

title: Countries with the youngest voting age
prompt: Which countries allow their citizens to vote in national elections at the youngest age?

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Suffrage / Wikipedia — Voting age

note: Voting age for general national elections. Some countries (e.g. Greece) have a slightly older presidential voting age; some (e.g. Bosnia) permit 16 for employed youth only. Rank groups by age, then alphabetically within a tier.
disclaimer: Voting age for general national elections. Some countries (e.g. Greece) have a slightly older presidential voting age; some (e.g. Bosnia) permit 16 for employed youth only. Rank groups by age, then alphabetically within a tier.

title: Most Nobel Peace Prize laureates
prompt: Name the countries whose citizens (or organizations headquartered there) have won the most Nobel Peace Prizes.

source.name: Nobel Foundation — Nobel Peace Prize laureates

disclaimer: Counts individual laureates and organizations by primary country of citizenship / headquarters. Dual-citizen laureates are counted for both countries.
trivia: The United States leads by a wide margin thanks to a long line of presidents (Roosevelt, Wilson, Carter, Obama) and civil-rights figures (King). The International Committee of the Red Cross has won the Peace Prize three separate times — more than any individual.

title: Most WWII total deaths
prompt: Name the countries that suffered the most total deaths (military + civilian) during World War II.

source.name: Wikipedia — World War II casualties (aggregating Ellman & Maksudov, Krivosheev, USHMM)

disclaimer: Total deaths include military KIA, civilian war-related deaths, and Holocaust victims attributed by prewar residence. Figures use commonly cited mid-range estimates; scholarly ranges vary widely for the USSR and China.
trivia: The Soviet Union's ~27 million dead is roughly 14% of its 1940 population. Poland lost about 17% of its prewar population — the highest per-capita loss of any country in the war.

title: Most WWI total deaths
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total deaths (military + civilian) in the First World War.

source.name: Wikipedia — World War I casualties (aggregating official government archives)

disclaimer: Uses mid-range historical estimates. Ottoman figures include Armenian genocide deaths as commonly aggregated. Successor-state codes used where the belligerent state no longer exists (Russian Empire → Russia, Austria-Hungary → Austria).
trivia: Germany and Russia each lost roughly two million soldiers — more than the entire prewar populations of some smaller belligerents. France mobilized ~8 million men and lost about 1 in 6.

title: Major Allied powers in WWII
prompt: Name the countries that fought as major Allied powers during World War II.

source.name: Wikipedia — Allies of World War II

disclaimer: Ranking uses the conventional Big Four / Big Five ordering and then approximate mobilized-force size among other major contributors. Excludes governments-in-exile and post-1945 combatants.
trivia: Brazil was the only independent South American country to send ground troops to Europe — the Brazilian Expeditionary Force fought in Italy in 1944-45. Mongolia declared war on Japan in the final days and its cavalry participated in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria.

title: Axis powers and co-belligerents in WWII
prompt: Name the countries that fought on the Axis side (or as Axis co-belligerents) during World War II.

source.name: Wikipedia — Axis powers

disclaimer: Ranks 1-3 are the Tripartite Pact core; remaining entries are ordered by approximate military contribution. Includes co-belligerents (Finland) and puppet/client states in their modern country code. Vichy France is coded under France; Manchukuo under China.
trivia: Finland fought the Soviet Union alongside Germany but never signed the Tripartite Pact and refused to hand over its Jewish population — its wartime status is often described as "co-belligerent" rather than fully Axis.

title: Oldest continuously inhabited civilizations
prompt: Name the countries with the earliest recorded civilizations still associated with their modern territory.

source.name: Wikipedia — Cradle of civilization (aggregating UNESCO and archaeological consensus)

disclaimer: Dates are approximate start of urban/state-level civilization on the modern country's territory, not modern nation-state founding. Sources vary by up to a few centuries; conventional archaeological consensus used.
trivia: Iraq (Mesopotamia) is home to the world's earliest cities — Uruk and Ur date to before 4000 BC. San Marino, founded in 301 AD, is the world's oldest continuously existing republic.

title: Largest colonial empires (by peak territory)
prompt: Name the countries that ruled the largest colonial empires at their peak extent.

source.name: Wikipedia — List of largest empires (aggregating Rein Taagepera, Turchin)

disclaimer: Peak territorial extent of overseas or contiguous colonial empire under a single metropolitan power. Land area in millions of square kilometres.
trivia: The British Empire covered nearly a quarter of the world's land surface in 1920 — the largest in history by area. Portugal held its first colony (Ceuta, 1415) and its last (Macau, until 1999) — the longest-running colonial empire.

title: Longest continuous royal dynasties
prompt: Name the countries with the longest continuous monarchical dynasty (single unbroken line).

source.name: Wikipedia — List of longest-reigning dynasties

disclaimer: Length measured from the legendary or historically attested founding of the current dynasty to the present or its abolition. Some early dates are traditional / legendary rather than firmly documented.
trivia: Japan's Imperial House traces itself to Emperor Jimmu in 660 BC — by tradition, the world's oldest continuous hereditary monarchy. Denmark's House of Glücksburg is the oldest currently reigning European royal line.

answers.value: House of Orange-Nassau — since 1815 as kings
House of Windsor / prior lines to 1066
House of Glücksburg / prior lines to c. 935

title: Countries never colonized by European powers
prompt: Name the countries that were never colonized or made a formal protectorate by a European power.

source.name: Wikipedia — List of countries that were never colonized by Europeans

disclaimer: Definitions vary. Includes countries that avoided formal European rule or protectorate status, even if briefly occupied (Ethiopia 1936-41, Thailand WWII). Excludes countries that lost formal sovereignty via protectorate treaties. Ordering is roughly by strength of the "never colonized" claim.
trivia: Ethiopia famously defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896 — the first decisive African victory over a European colonizer. Thailand's kings played France and Britain off each other to keep Siam as a buffer state.

answers.value: Founded 1847 by freed slaves; never colonized
Protected state but never formal colony
North Yemen never colonized (Ottoman then independent)

title: Countries occupied longest during WWII
prompt: Name the countries that spent the longest continuous period under Axis occupation during World War II.

source.name: Wikipedia — German-occupied Europe / Japanese-occupied territories

disclaimer: Measures continuous occupation duration by any Axis power. Some countries counted from Japanese invasion in 1937 predating the European war. Ranges use commonly cited liberation dates.
trivia: Manchuria was under Japanese control as the puppet state of Manchukuo from 1931 — nearly 14 years, longer than any European occupation. The Channel Islands (UK) were the only British territory occupied by Germany, from June 1940 to May 1945.

title: Most Facebook users
prompt: Name the countries with the largest number of Facebook users.

source.name: DataReportal — Digital 2024 Global Overview / Meta Ads audience data
source.asOf: 2024 (Meta ad-reach data compiled by DataReportal / We Are Social)

disclaimer: Values are Meta's own advertising-reach estimates (users age 13+), which DataReportal republishes each quarter. Facebook is blocked in mainland China, so China is excluded from the ranking.
trivia: India passed the US around 2017 and has held the #1 slot ever since despite Facebook's slower growth there than on WhatsApp.
asOfDate: 2024 (Meta ad-reach data compiled by DataReportal / We Are Social)

title: Most YouTube users
prompt: Name the countries with the largest YouTube user bases.

source.name: DataReportal — Digital 2024 (Global Statshot) / Google Ads audience data

disclaimer: Ad-reach potential for users age 18+ as reported through Google's advertising tools; YouTube is blocked in mainland China.
trivia: YouTube reaches nearly 100% of India's online population — even higher than Facebook's or WhatsApp's local footprints.

title: Most WhatsApp users
prompt: Name the countries with the most WhatsApp users.

source.name: DataReportal — Digital 2024 / Statista WhatsApp user estimates

disclaimer: Monthly active users; WhatsApp is banned in mainland China and heavily restricted in the UAE for voice calling.
trivia: Brazil is often called the world's most WhatsApp-obsessed country — nearly the entire adult online population uses it.

title: Most X (Twitter) users
prompt: Name the countries with the largest X (formerly Twitter) user bases.

source.name: DataReportal — Digital 2024 / Statista X audience data

disclaimer: Ad-reach potential for users age 13+ as reported through X's ad tools; X is blocked in mainland China and periodically restricted in a handful of other markets.
trivia: Japan is X's second-largest market and one of the few where it beats every rival short-form text network.

title: Most LinkedIn members
prompt: Name the countries with the largest number of LinkedIn members.

source.name: DataReportal — Digital 2024 / LinkedIn Ads audience insights

disclaimer: Registered LinkedIn members age 18+ as reported through LinkedIn's ad tools; LinkedIn is blocked in mainland China (a separate 'InCareer' product was shuttered in 2023).
trivia: India is on track to overtake the US as LinkedIn's largest market before 2030 — the fastest-growing country in the platform's history.

title: Most Snapchat users
prompt: Name the countries with the most Snapchat users.

source.name: DataReportal — Digital 2024 / Snap Inc. ad audience data

disclaimer: Snap's own ad-reach potential (age 13+); Snapchat has particularly strong penetration in the Gulf and in France relative to population.
trivia: Saudi Arabia's per-capita Snapchat use is the highest in the world — the app functions there almost like a national broadcast channel.

title: Highest social media penetration
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of population actively using social media.

source.name: DataReportal / We Are Social / Meltwater — Digital 2024

disclaimer: Active social-media user identities as a percentage of total population. Very small nations (population under 1M) and territories are excluded to avoid single-platform outliers.
trivia: The UAE routinely tops the DataReportal list — over 99% of the online population there uses at least one social platform.

title: Most daily time on social media
prompt: Name the countries whose users spend the most time on social media per day.

source.name: DataReportal / GWI — Digital 2024

disclaimer: GWI panel of internet users age 16-64. Time spent covers all social platforms combined including messaging apps like WhatsApp.
trivia: Nigerian and Filipino users have alternated at the top of GWI's list for most of the past decade.

title: Most Android smartphone users
prompt: Name the countries with the most Android smartphone users.

source.name: Statista Market Insights — Smartphone users by OS

disclaimer: Estimated active Android device users; based on StatCounter share of smartphones applied to national smartphone user totals.
trivia: Android holds over 95% smartphone share in India — the platform's single most dominant large market.

title: Most iOS (iPhone) users
prompt: Name the countries with the most active iOS (iPhone) users.

source.name: Statista Market Insights / StatCounter smartphone OS share applied to national handset totals

disclaimer: Estimated active iPhone users derived from StatCounter mobile-OS share and national smartphone user totals; excludes iPads and iPods.
trivia: Apple's home country has the highest iOS smartphone share of any large market — well over half of active US phones are iPhones.

title: Largest manufacturing value-added
prompt: Name the countries with the largest manufacturing value-added output.

source.name: World Bank — Manufacturing, value added (current US$)
source.asOf: 2023 (World Bank / UN Statistics Division national accounts)

disclaimer: Manufacturing value added in current USD, following ISIC Rev.4 divisions 10-33 (excludes mining, utilities, and construction). Latest World Bank figures for the 2023 reference year.
trivia: China's manufacturing value-added is roughly equal to that of the next three countries combined, and about 2.5x that of the United States.
asOfDate: 2023 (World Bank / UN Statistics Division national accounts)

title: Largest auto producers by vehicles made
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most motor vehicles (cars plus commercial vehicles).

source.name: OICA — International Organization of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers

disclaimer: Total light and commercial vehicle production (cars, LCVs, trucks, buses) as reported by OICA member associations. Includes all vehicles assembled in-country regardless of the brand's home nationality.
trivia: China has led global vehicle production every year since 2009, when it overtook Japan; its 2023 output of 30 million vehicles exceeded the combined production of the next three countries.

title: Largest electric vehicle producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most battery-electric and plug-in hybrid passenger vehicles.

source.name: IEA — Global EV Outlook

disclaimer: Combined battery-electric (BEV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) passenger car production. Country of production, not brand nationality.
trivia: China alone produced roughly six out of every ten plug-in vehicles rolling off assembly lines worldwide in 2023.

title: Largest shipbuilders
prompt: Name the countries that build the most commercial ships by tonnage.

source.name: Clarksons Research / UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport

disclaimer: Ranked by gross tonnage of commercial ship completions in 2023. Three countries dominate the global order book with more than 90% share combined.
trivia: South Korea's Hyundai Heavy Industries is the single largest shipbuilder in the world, and Korea leads in high-value LNG carrier orders while China leads in bulk tonnage.

title: Largest semiconductor producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest share of global semiconductor manufacturing capacity.

source.name: SIA / BCG — Government Incentives and US Competitiveness in Semiconductor Manufacturing

disclaimer: Share of world installed wafer fabrication capacity (all technology nodes, in wafer starts per month equivalent). Includes memory, logic, analog, and specialty semiconductors.
trivia: Taiwan produces roughly 90% of the world's most advanced (sub-7nm) logic chips, all fabricated by TSMC.

title: Largest smartphone producers
prompt: Name the countries that assemble the most smartphones.

source.name: Counterpoint Research / IDC Smartphone Manufacturing Tracker

disclaimer: Units of finished smartphones assembled in-country in 2023. Two countries account for roughly 90% of global assembly, with India rapidly expanding under production-linked incentive schemes.
trivia: India overtook Vietnam as the world's second-largest smartphone maker around 2022 as Apple and Samsung shifted assembly out of China; the majority of iPhones sold in the US are now made in India.

title: Largest pharmaceutical producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest pharmaceutical manufacturing output by value.

source.name: EFPIA / IQVIA — The Pharmaceutical Industry in Figures

disclaimer: Value of pharmaceutical production (finished formulations plus active pharmaceutical ingredients) in current USD. Includes both branded and generic products.
trivia: Switzerland's per-capita pharmaceutical output is the highest in the world by a wide margin, driven almost entirely by Roche and Novartis.

title: Largest chemical producers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest chemical industry sales.

source.name: CEFIC — The European Chemical Industry Council, Facts & Figures

disclaimer: Total chemical industry sales in current USD, covering basic chemicals, specialty chemicals, consumer chemicals, and polymers. Excludes pharmaceuticals (tracked separately).
trivia: China's chemical industry alone is now larger than the combined output of the entire European Union, having overtaken the EU in the mid-2010s.

title: Largest cement producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most cement.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Cement

disclaimer: Hydraulic cement production in metric tons. Values for the top producer are USGS estimates rounded to the nearest 10 million tons.
trivia: China has produced more cement in the past three years than the United States did in the entire 20th century.

title: Highest robot density in manufacturing
prompt: Name the countries with the highest number of industrial robots per 10,000 manufacturing workers.

source.name: IFR — International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics Report

disclaimer: Operational industrial robots per 10,000 employees in the manufacturing sector. Only countries with a manufacturing base large enough for IFR to publish a density figure are included.
trivia: South Korea has led the IFR density ranking every year since 2010; Singapore's high figure is heavily concentrated in the semiconductor and electronics sector.

title: Most Golden Globe wins by country of production
prompt: Name the countries with the most Golden Globe Award wins across film and television categories (by country of production).

source.name: Hollywood Foreign Press Association — Golden Globes winners database

disclaimer: Aggregates all competitive Golden Globe wins in film and TV since 1944, credited to the primary country of production. Co-productions are attributed to the lead producing country as listed by the HFPA.
trivia: The Best Foreign Language Film / Best Non-English Language Motion Picture category (established 1948) has been won by films from over 30 different countries, more national diversity than any single Oscar category.

title: Highest cinema admissions per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita movie theater admissions (tickets sold per person per year).

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Feature Films and Cinema data / MPA Theme Report

disclaimer: Admissions divided by resident population. Only countries with an established cinema exhibition sector (>=100 screens or >=1M annual admissions) are included, to avoid microstate distortions.
trivia: Iceland has consistently ranked as one of the world's top per-capita moviegoing nations for decades, at times exceeding 5 tickets per person per year despite having fewer than 40 total cinema screens nationwide.

title: Most cinema screens by country
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total number of cinema screens in operation.

source.name: MPA Theatrical and Home Entertainment Market Environment (THEME) Report / UNESCO cinema data

disclaimer: Counts all commercial cinema screens (multiplex, single-screen, drive-in). Excludes non-commercial venues (film clubs, universities). China and the US together account for a large majority of the global screen count.
trivia: China overtook the United States as the country with the most cinema screens around 2016, and roughly doubled its screen count between 2015 and 2020 — the fastest cinema-infrastructure expansion in film history.

title: Most Grammy Album of the Year winners by artist nationality
prompt: Name the countries with the most Grammy Album of the Year wins, credited by the primary artist's country of citizenship.

source.name: Recording Academy — GRAMMY.com winners database (Album of the Year)
source.asOf: Through the 66th Grammy Awards (2024, Taylor Swift — Midnights)

disclaimer: Credits the winning act's primary nationality; for groups with mixed nationalities the country most associated with the act is used (e.g. Fleetwood Mac -> US). Established 1959.
trivia: Taylor Swift became the first artist ever to win Album of the Year four times, at the 66th Grammys in 2024, breaking a tie with Frank Sinatra, Paul Simon, and Stevie Wonder.
asOfDate: Through the 66th Grammy Awards (2024, Taylor Swift — Midnights)

title: Most Billboard Hot 100 hits by non-English-language music origin
prompt: Name the countries whose artists have produced the most Billboard Hot 100 chart entries in the streaming era (2015-2024), by artist country of origin.

source.name: Billboard — Hot 100 chart archive / Luminate year-end reports

disclaimer: Counts distinct songs charting on the Hot 100 credited to the lead artist's country of citizenship. Includes English- and non-English-language songs. Featured artists count for their credited home country.
trivia: In 2012, PSY's 'Gangnam Style' reached #2 on the Hot 100, the highest a Korean-language track had ever charted at the time; BTS became the first Korean act to hit #1 in 2020 with 'Dynamite'.

title: Highest streaming music subscribers per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest number of paid music streaming subscribers per capita.

source.name: IFPI Engaging with Music report / MIDiA Research streaming subscriber estimates

disclaimer: Paid subscribers to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music Premium, Tidal, Deezer, and equivalents, divided by resident population. Only markets with >=1M subscribers included.
trivia: The Nordic countries pioneered paid music streaming globally — Sweden, home of Spotify, had over 50% of its adult population paying for a streaming service years before the US crossed that threshold.

title: Highest podcast listener rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of the population who listen to podcasts at least monthly.

source.name: Reuters Institute Digital News Report — Podcast use / Edison Research global podcast surveys

disclaimer: Share of adults (18+) who listened to at least one podcast in the past month, per Reuters/Edison survey methodology. Rates vary with survey framing; only countries with directly comparable Reuters DNR data included.
trivia: Ireland and Sweden have consistently ranked in the top 5 podcast-listening countries worldwide, both crossing 40% monthly listenership before most European neighbours reached 30%.

title: Most Cannes Best Actor and Actress winners by country
prompt: Name the countries with the most Cannes Film Festival Best Actor and Best Actress prize winners combined (by performer's country of nationality).

source.name: Festival de Cannes — Best Performance prize archive

disclaimer: Combines Cannes Best Actor (Prix d'interpretation masculine) and Best Actress (Prix d'interpretation feminine) winners since 1946, credited by the actor's country of citizenship at the time of the win. Shared prizes count once per country.
trivia: Isabelle Huppert, Vanessa Redgrave, Barbara Hershey, and Holly Hunter are among a select group of Cannes Best Actress winners; the record for most Cannes Best Actress wins is held by Barbara Hershey and Vanessa Redgrave with two apiece.

title: Most FIAPF-accredited international film festivals hosted
prompt: Name the countries hosting the most FIAPF-accredited (International Federation of Film Producers Associations) international film festivals.

source.name: FIAPF — Accredited Festivals Directory

disclaimer: Counts FIAPF-accredited festivals across all four categories (Competitive Feature Film, Competitive Specialised, Non-Competitive Feature Film, Documentary and Short). Only festivals holding active FIAPF accreditation as of 2024 are included.
trivia: FIAPF was founded in 1933 and today accredits fewer than 50 festivals worldwide — Cannes, Venice, Berlin, Locarno, Karlovy Vary, Shanghai, San Sebastian, and Tokyo are among the top-tier 'Competitive Feature Film' festivals.

title: Most linear TV channels by country
prompt: Name the countries with the largest number of linear (broadcast + cable + satellite) television channels in operation.

source.name: European Audiovisual Observatory MAVISE database / OFCOM / FCC / national broadcast regulators

disclaimer: Includes all licensed linear TV channels (national, regional, cable, satellite, IPTV) reporting to national regulators. Excludes web-only streamers and pure video-on-demand services. Regional variants (e.g. multiple BBC One feeds) count as separate licensed services where the regulator lists them.
trivia: The United States has the most licensed TV stations of any country, with over 1,700 licensed full-power stations plus tens of thousands of low-power and translator stations tracked by the FCC.

title: Largest air forces by aircraft count
prompt: Name the countries with the most military aircraft of all types in service.

source.name: World Air Forces / Flight Global (IISS Military Balance corroborated)

disclaimer: Counts total active military aircraft (fixed-wing and rotary combined, all roles). Trainers, transports, and helicopters included.
trivia: The United States operates roughly a quarter of the world's military aircraft, more than the next three countries combined.

title: Largest navies by ship count
prompt: Name the countries with the most vessels in their naval fleets.

source.name: IISS Military Balance / Global Firepower fleet totals

disclaimer: Total naval assets include warships, submarines, patrol craft, and auxiliary vessels. Not weighted by tonnage — a patrol boat and an aircraft carrier both count as one.
trivia: North Korea's massive count is dominated by hundreds of small coastal patrol and midget-submarine craft, not blue-water warships.

title: Largest navies by tonnage
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total displacement of naval warships.

source.name: IISS Military Balance / naval tonnage compilations

disclaimer: Aggregate battle-force displacement in tonnes; carriers and large surface combatants dominate the total.
trivia: The US Navy's tonnage advantage comes almost entirely from its 11 supercarriers, each displacing ~100,000 tonnes fully loaded.

title: Most active aircraft carriers
prompt: Name the countries operating the most aircraft carriers.

source.name: IISS Military Balance / national navy inventories

disclaimer: Includes fixed-wing carriers and dedicated helicopter carriers / amphibious assault ships capable of operating jump-jets (LHD/LHA type).
trivia: The US operates 11 nuclear-powered supercarriers plus 9 amphibious assault ships larger than most nations' flagships.

title: Most military bases abroad
prompt: Name the countries with the most military installations located in foreign nations.

source.name: Al Jazeera / Politico compilations from public MoD data

disclaimer: Includes major and minor overseas installations, forward operating sites, and lily-pad bases. Excludes embassies and diplomatic security posts.
trivia: The US operates roughly 750 overseas bases in over 80 countries — more than the rest of the world combined.

title: Largest reserve military forces
prompt: Name the countries with the most reserve military personnel available for mobilization.

source.name: IISS Military Balance 2024

disclaimer: Reserve personnel available for mobilization. Excludes paramilitary. Some countries include large militia formations in their reserve counts.
trivia: Vietnam's 5-million reserve figure reflects its universal-conscription doctrine of a 'people's war'.

title: Largest paramilitary forces
prompt: Name the countries with the highest paramilitary personnel counts.

source.name: IISS Military Balance 2024

disclaimer: Paramilitary includes gendarmerie, border guards, internal-security troops, and coast guards operating under state authority — separate from the regular armed forces.
trivia: China's People's Armed Police alone numbers ~660,000, and Russia's Rosgvardiya is a ~340,000-strong internal army distinct from the Ministry of Defence.

title: Most peacekeeping troops contributed to UN
prompt: Name the countries contributing the most uniformed personnel to active UN peacekeeping missions.

source.name: UN Peacekeeping — Troop and Police Contributors

disclaimer: Uniformed personnel (troops, police, experts, staff officers) currently deployed to UN missions. Excludes non-UN coalition deployments.
trivia: South Asian nations plus Rwanda have consistently topped the UN contributor list for over a decade, providing about half of all peacekeepers.

title: Highest active military per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest ratio of active-duty military personnel to total population.

source.name: IISS Military Balance / World Bank population data

disclaimer: Active-duty personnel per 1,000 residents. Microstates and city-states with garrison-only forces excluded.
trivia: North Korea's ratio implies roughly 1 in 20 citizens is in uniform — an economically crushing proportion sustained by universal long-service conscription.

title: Highest military dead in wars since 1945
prompt: Name the countries with the highest combatant military death tolls in conflicts since the end of WWII.

source.name: Correlates of War / PRIO Battle Deaths Dataset

disclaimer: Uniformed combatant deaths only (not civilian casualties). Vietnam War, Korean War, Iran-Iraq War, and Russo-Ukrainian War dominate the totals.
trivia: The Iran-Iraq War (1980-88) killed an estimated 500,000+ Iranian and 250,000+ Iraqi soldiers — one of the deadliest post-WWII conflicts.

title: Largest iron ore producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most iron ore by usable ore tonnage.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Iron Ore

disclaimer: USGS figures are usable ore (not iron content). Estimates in million metric tonnes.
trivia: Australia and Brazil together supply more than half of the world's seaborne iron ore trade, feeding China's steel mills.

title: Largest steel producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most crude steel.

source.name: World Steel Association — World Steel in Figures

disclaimer: Crude steel output in million metric tonnes.
trivia: China alone produces more crude steel than the rest of the world combined, a dominance held since the mid-2000s.

title: Largest aluminum producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most primary aluminum.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Aluminum

disclaimer: Primary smelter output in million metric tonnes, excluding secondary/recycled aluminum.
trivia: Aluminum smelting is energy-intensive; Iceland and Norway punch above their weight thanks to cheap hydro and geothermal power.

title: Largest nickel producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most nickel by ore content.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Nickel

disclaimer: Mine production, nickel content in thousand metric tonnes.
trivia: Indonesia's ban on unprocessed nickel ore exports drove a massive smelting build-out, and it now supplies about half the world's mined nickel.

title: Largest lithium producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most lithium from mining and brines.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Lithium

disclaimer: Mine production, lithium content in tonnes. Excludes US which USGS withholds for proprietary reasons.
trivia: Australia extracts lithium from hard-rock spodumene mines while Chile and Argentina harvest it from brine salars — different chemistry, same battery boom.

title: Largest cobalt producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most cobalt by ore content.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Cobalt

disclaimer: Mine production, cobalt content in tonnes.
trivia: The Democratic Republic of the Congo mines roughly three-quarters of the world's cobalt, most of it as a byproduct of copper.

title: Largest uranium producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most uranium.

source.name: World Nuclear Association — World Uranium Mining Production

disclaimer: Uranium mine output in tonnes of U (uranium metal equivalent).
trivia: Kazakhstan mines uranium mostly via in-situ leaching, a lower-cost method that pushed it past Canada and Australia in the 2010s.

title: Largest diamond producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most rough diamonds by carat volume.

source.name: Kimberley Process — Rough Diamond Statistics

disclaimer: Rough diamond production in millions of carats (volume, not value).
trivia: By value the picture changes: Botswana's Jwaneng mine produces fewer carats than Russia's Yakutia mines, but far higher gem quality per carat.

title: Largest coal producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most coal.

source.name: EIA — International Coal Data

disclaimer: Total coal production (bituminous, lignite, anthracite) in million short tons.
trivia: China burns more than half of the world's coal, and its domestic mines account for roughly the same share of global output.

title: Largest proven oil reserves
prompt: Name the countries with the largest proven crude oil reserves.

source.name: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin

disclaimer: Proven reserves in billions of barrels. Venezuela's figure includes extra-heavy Orinoco Belt crude.
trivia: Venezuela overtook Saudi Arabia atop the reserves league in 2011 after reclassifying Orinoco Belt heavy crude — production tells a very different story.

title: Largest e-commerce market (revenue)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total e-commerce revenue.

source.name: Statista Market Insights — eCommerce

disclaimer: B2C online sales of physical goods only, excludes digital services and B2B. USD at current exchange rates.
trivia: China alone accounts for roughly half of global online retail sales — more than the next five markets combined.

title: Highest e-commerce revenue per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest online retail revenue per capita.

source.name: Statista Market Insights — eCommerce

disclaimer: Annual e-commerce revenue divided by population. B2C physical goods only, USD.
trivia: Wealthy small economies dominate per-capita rankings even though their absolute markets are dwarfed by the US and China.

title: Most McDonald's locations
prompt: Name the countries with the most McDonald's restaurants.

source.name: McDonald's Corporation annual report and country disclosures

disclaimer: Total restaurant count (company-operated and franchised). Corporate reporting rounds to nearest ten in some markets.
trivia: About 40% of all McDonald's restaurants worldwide are in a single country — the United States.

title: Most Starbucks locations
prompt: Name the countries with the most Starbucks coffee stores.

source.name: Starbucks Corporation 10-K filing and store counts

disclaimer: Total company-operated and licensed stores. Starbucks' two largest markets together account for more than 60% of global stores.
trivia: Starbucks did not open a store in Italy — the country whose espresso culture inspired Howard Schultz's original concept — until 2018.

title: Most 7-Eleven convenience stores
prompt: Name the countries with the most 7-Eleven convenience stores.

source.name: Seven & i Holdings annual report
